title: Admin CLI: usenet-ipfs-ctl
description:
A command-line tool that talks to the admin HTTP endpoint, so operators do not need to curl JSON by hand.

Why this issue exists:
The admin HTTP endpoint exposes useful operations (/health, /stats, /peers, /log-tip, /metrics, /reload) but requires curl and manual JSON parsing to use. Operators expect a purpose-built CLI for day-to-day tasks.

Scope:
New binary: usenet-ipfs-ctl

Commands:
- ctl status [--host] — show health, uptime, article count, peer count
- ctl peers — list connected peers with address, last-seen, article exchange count
- ctl groups — list subscribed groups with article count and log tip CID
- ctl log-tip <group> — print the current log tip CID for a group
- ctl reload — trigger config reload (POST /admin/reload), print what changed
- ctl metrics — print Prometheus text output (passthrough)
- ctl version — print daemon version and build info

Global flags:
- --host / -H: admin endpoint base URL (default http://127.0.0.1:9090)
- --token: bearer token for authenticated admin endpoints
- --json: output raw JSON instead of formatted table

The binary is thin: it makes HTTP calls to the admin endpoint and formats the response. No business logic.

Acceptance criteria:
- ctl status prints a human-readable summary of daemon health
- ctl peers --json outputs the same JSON as GET /admin/peers
- ctl reload prints the list of changed config fields
- ctl connects to a custom --host without code changes
- All commands exit non-zero and print an error if the admin endpoint is unreachable
